prompt:
A real documentary photograph taken on a commercial water damage job in an open-plan office. Portrait orientation, shot vertically down the length of the floor so the ceiling grid and the carpet both run away from the camera.

Standing water across low-pile commercial carpet tiles, some tiles lifted and stacked against a desk leg. Two yellow air movers on the floor angled along the skirting trunking, and one LGR dehumidifier with a lay-flat duct. A technician in a navy polo and knee pads crouched mid-frame reading a moisture meter against the base of a plasterboard partition — working, not posing, face partly turned away. Workstations still in place with monitors and chairs pushed aside, cable trays visible, a few cardboard document boxes moved up onto a desktop.

Lighting is ordinary office fluorescent troffers, flat and slightly green, with grey daylight through a window at the far end. No sunbeams, no golden hour, no lens flare.

Deliberately unglamorous: scuffed carpet, a dented filing cabinet, a coiled extension lead taped to the floor, water stains creeping up the partition, a smudged ceiling tile. Surfaces should look used — not new, not polished, not reflective.

Shot on a 28mm lens at f/4, handheld, mild sensor noise, natural white balance left uncorrected. Plain realistic colour, no grading. No text, no logos, no watermarks.

3:4 portrait, roughly 1200 × 1600. Water has faint dull broken reflections, no glossy mirror sheen. Believable technician anatomy and physical equipment placement.
